title: SSO & Least-Privilege Access Review w/ NimbleGuard Systems
summary: Redwood and NimbleGuard run through SSO (SAML/SCIM) setup options, SCIM attribute mapping, RBAC and least-privilege patterns, audit log requirements, and KMS integration. NimbleGuard is evaluating hosted vs private deployment for compliance reasons and needs a SCIM pilot + security docs and a role mapping template.
topics: Data residency and private deployment considerations
action_items: Samira Patel - Send Nexus security pack (SOC2 + ISO summaries + network diagram) by 2027-06-14
Diego Morales - Draft sample SCIM attribute map + group-to-role mapping spreadsheet by 2027-06-18
NimbleGuard (Rina) - Share current Okta org test tenant + sample user list by 2027-06-16
Ava Lin - Schedule technical workshop for SCIM end-to-end provisioning (2hr) week of 2027-06-21
next_steps: Redwood to share security pack and architecture diagram
Run SCIM provisioning pilot using NimbleGuard test tenant
Confirm deployment mode preference (hosted with VPC vs private) after pilot
Schedule integration workshop to exercise role creation and JIT access flows
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-06-11 15:00 UTC | Duration: 53 min | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Ava (Redwood SE), Paul (NimbleGuard InfoSec), Rina (Platform), Marcelo (SRE), Leah (IAM)

Summary: quick run through SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, focus on least-privilege RBAC mapping and audit log retention + KMS. Customer wants to validate SCIM flows and ensure audit trails meet SOC2 requirements, also asks about key rotation and HSM/KMS integration.

00:00:00 - Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll do a 90 second intro. Um Redwood helps run inference but also we have a pretty full security and deployment playbook so we can support hosted and private installs.
00:00:17 - Paul: Yep thanks Samira. We're looking to land SSO and SCIM provisioning and map groups to least-priv roles. Also need to be sure logs go to our SIEM and KMS policies cover key rotation, so yeah lots to cover.
00:00:32 - Diego: Great, quick clarifying question: do you currently manage users in Okta or Azure AD? or a mixture?
00:00:38 - Rina: Okta primary, we do have a handful of external service accounts in Azure AD but for this pilot OKTA is the source of truth.
00:00:47 - Samira: Awesome. For SAML we support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, metadata exchange is straightforward. For SCIM we support group sync, user create/update/deactivate, and custom attribute mapping.
00:01:02 - Leah: How's the group mapping look? we have a pretty granular role model, we try to do least privilege; engineers get token-level access, SREs can run evals, and InfoSec has audit-read only.
00:01:14 - Ava: Yep you'll map groups to Redwood roles. We usually recommend creating permission slices, like read-only, inference-run, admin, and then attach those to groups from Okta. And we can show a sample mapping.
00:01:28 - Marcelo: What about service accounts? we need programmatic access for CI/CD with long-lived keys, can that be scoped?
00:01:36 - Diego: We support service principals and token-scoped roles. We also have short-lived tokens for automation that can be bound to a service account with limited permissions. So yes you can scope them.
00:01:49 - Paul: Audit logs, retention, and forwarding: SOC2 wants immutable logs for 12 months, sometimes 24 depending on module. Can we push logs to our Splunk?
00:01:58 - Samira: Yes, log forwarding to syslog/forwarders or direct S3 buckets is supported. We can ship structured audit events with user id, action, token id, resource id, and we keep an append-only chain. We'll include sample events in the pack.
00:02:12 - Rina: How about attribute mapping with SCIM? we have custom attributes like team_code and entitlement_flag, can we sync those?
00:02:20 - Ava: We can sync custom attributes as long as Okta exposes them in the SCIM profile. We do attribute normalization on ingest and you can map them to role selectors in our mapping table. We have a spreadsheet template we usually share.
00:02:35 - Leah: Any caveats with SAML sessions and token expiry? we want 1hr sessions and reauth for privileged actions.
00:02:42 - Diego: Session lifetime is configurable; SAML assertion TTL can be set from your IdP and on our side we honor the assertion and then issue session tokens with configurable TTL. For privileged actions we recommend MFA-on-demand or step-up with shorter TTLs.
00:02:57 - Paul: KMS and HSM — do you integrate with customer KMS? we use AWS KMS with an external key policy and rotation. We also need envelope encryption for model artifacts.
00:03:06 - Samira: Yes we have integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer-managed keys in HSMs. For model artifacts we recommend envelope encryption; the platform supports customer key wrapping and rotate keys per compliance cycles. We'll provide the KMS policy template.
00:03:21 - Marcelo: Is there an option for on-prem or VPC private deployment for data residency? latency is also a factor for us.
00:03:28 - Samira: We offer private deployments and VPC options; private installs let you keep all logs in your network and use your key material. We'll go through pros/cons: hosted is faster to stand up, private gives you full control for audit and residency.
00:03:41 - Rina: How do we prove separation of duties for SOC2? e.g., admin vs infra vs app teams.
00:03:48 - Ava: RBAC with audit trails, role change approvals, and SSO provisioning flows are usually demonstrated in the audit. We can show role change logs, SCIM provisioning events, and admin console access logs.
00:04:02 - Paul: Can we restrict who can create service accounts? that's been a big control for us.
00:04:08 - Diego: Yes, you can gate service account creation to an admin role and require a JIRA ticket id to create certain privileged accounts; we can attach a required tag and enforce it in provisioning flows.
00:04:23 - Rina: Do you support SCIM patch semantics vs full replace? we prefer patch for group membership changes.
00:04:29 - Ava: We support PATCH operations for group membership and incremental updates, that reduces churn and race conditions.
00:04:36 - Leah: What about replication lag? our teams expect near-real-time group sync.
00:04:41 - Diego: Typical group sync runs under 30 seconds for small orgs; for large orgs we recommend incremental sync and delta polling. For pivots we have a change stream approach if you need push-based sync.
00:04:56 - Paul: For the pilot can you show the SCIM create user flow and then deprovision? we need to see orphaned account handling.
00:05:04 - Samira: Absolutely. We'll do a demo in the integration workshop: create user in Okta, SCIM create in Redwood, assign group -> role, then deprovision and show revoke and audit event.
00:05:16 - Marcelo: Encryption at rest: are logs encrypted server-side and do you support customer-managed keys for logs?
00:05:24 - Diego: Yes logs encrypted at rest; for hosted we offer customer-managed keys to encrypt backups and audit exports. For private installs you manage KMS entirely.
00:05:34 - Rina: Data residency: can we pin model metadata and logs to eu-west-1 only?
00:05:39 - Ava: You can set region constraints; for hosted we can pin tenant data to a region, though some compute may be routed for capacity—if you need strict residency we recommend a private deployment.
00:05:53 - Paul: Are there any gotchas with group-to-role mapping where Okta nested groups cause weird role explosion?
00:05:59 - Diego: Nested groups can expand cardinality; we usually flatten on ingest and have a policy for inheritance. We'll show options like explicit mapping, prefix rules, and exclude lists.
00:06:12 - Samira: Quick question for your timeline: you mentioned SOC2 readiness — are you already under audit or prepping?
00:06:19 - Paul: Preparing, audit kicks off in Q4. We want SCIM pilot, role mapping, and evidence of log forwarding in Q3.
00:06:26 - Samira: Good timing. We'll prioritize the SCIM pilot and send the security pack this week.
00:06:32 - Paul: Great. A couple of nitty gritty items — how are cross-tenant service accounts handled? we have partners that need limited access.
00:06:40 - Ava: We support cross-tenant roles via scoped API keys and OAuth clients; partner access can be scoped to specific endpoints and limited in time.
00:06:51 - Rina: Any support for Just-In-Time provisioning when someone requests elevated access?
00:06:56 - Diego: We have JIT flows via API to create ephemeral elevated sessions tied to an approval flow; that's ideal for break-glass scenarios.
00:07:06 - Leah: Do audit events include the assertion id from SAML so we can tie the action back to SSO?
00:07:10 - Diego: Yes we log assertion id, subject, and session id so auditors can trace user identity back to the IdP.
00:07:18 - Samira: Ok if nobody objects i'll pivot to some technical constraints around SCIM mappings and attribute naming — we sometimes see differences in Okta naming conventions that cause a little munging.
00:07:28 - Rina: yep we had that with another vendor, they'd expect "employeeNumber" but we used "emp_num".
00:07:32 - Ava: totally, that's why our template allows you to map Okta attributes to Redwood canonical attributes and transform case and format.
00:07:40 - Marcelo: About keys again — do you support external HSM with BYOK and rotation schedule triggers?
00:07:46 - Diego: Yes BYOK is supported; rotation is orchestrated by the customer's KMS and we support key versioning and rewrap. We'll show the rewrap flow in the KMS doc.
00:07:56 - Paul: For SOC2 we need evidence of separation of duties on RBAC changes. do you have approval workflows in the console?
00:08:03 - Ava: We have role change approvals built into the admin console and can require two-person approval for elevation. These actions are logged for audit.
00:08:14 - Samira: Any regulatory constraints around EU vs US data for you?
00:08:18 - Paul: EU-residency for personal data is a must, logs should remain in EU. Model weights can be in US if encrypted, but metadata and PII stays in EU.
00:08:28 - Diego: Understood, we'll note that and recommend private tenancy in EU or a hosted-eu pin.
00:08:36 - Leah: Are SAML metadata or certificates rotated automatically? we want a certificate rotation cadence.
00:08:42 - Ava: We support automated cert rotation if you let Redwood manage the SP key; if you manage it in your IdP, you control rotation. We recommend rotating every 12 months and have alerts prior to expiry.
00:08:55 - Rina: How does Redwood surface audit events? raw logs or structured events? we prefer structured JSON events for Splunk parsing.
00:09:03 - Diego: Structured JSON events with fields like event_type, actor, resource, before/after, and assertion_id. We can push to S3 or your SIEM collector.
00:09:13 - Paul: Ok for the pilot scope: SCIM group sync, SAML SSO test, role mapping for two roles, log forwarding to our Splunk test instance, and KMS proof-of-concept. timeline Q3.
00:09:25 - Samira: Sounds good. We'll produce a one-pager with the pilot plan and success criteria.
00:09:31 - Marcelo: Are there quotas or rate limits on SCIM calls? we want spike protection.
00:09:36 - Diego: There are rate limits but we can increase them for pilots; SCIM endpoints support batching to reduce calls.
00:09:45 - Rina: How do you handle orphaned accounts when a user is removed in Okta but tokens are cached in the runtime?
00:09:52 - Ava: When SCIM deprovisions we invalidate sessions and revoke tokens; we also support a prefix blacklist for long-lived resources. We'll demonstrate in the workshop.
00:10:04 - Paul: Any red flags around compliance trackers? e.g., do you provide evidence packs for auditors?
00:10:09 - Samira: Yes we provide SOC2 and ISO summaries, audit logs, configuration snapshots, and runbook material. We'll attach those in the security pack.
00:10:18 - Leah: For role mapping template can you include examples of deny rules? we prefer explicit deny for certain endpoints.
00:10:24 - Diego: We support allow and deny rules in the policy language and can include example deny expressions in the mapping sheet.
00:10:33 - Paul: Great — one more on data residency: what if we need air-gapped environment for certain models?
00:10:39 - Samira: We offer on-prem private installs for air-gap scenarios; that would require an enterprise engagement. We'll outline requirements in the private deployment doc.
00:10:49 - Rina: Ok we're good to move to next steps.
00:10:52 - Samira: Quick recap: Redwood will send security pack, Diego will draft SCIM map, Ava will schedule workshop, NimbleGuard share Okta test tenant. Pilot plan doc will be shared. Any final Qs?
00:11:06 - Paul: No, just please include sample audit events and KMS policy snippets.
00:11:11 - Samira: will do. Thanks everyone.
00:11:14 - (meeting recorded ended)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-heard words (eg "K-V cache" for KV cache). Some names may be rendered slightly different by auto transcript. Links shared: security pack (link to redwood security packet), sample SCIM spreadsheet (link), pilot plan doc (link).
